row.question:
Based on the chest X-ray findings, which of the following best describes the anatomical relationship and reasoning for the observed mediastinal shift in Figure 1?

A) The mediastinal shift is due to right lung hyperexpansion and left-sided dextrocardia.
B) The mediastinal shift is caused by volume loss in the right hemithorax with compensatory left lung expansion.
C) The mediastinal shift is due to a mass in the right lung causing leftward displacement.
D) The mediastinal shift is due to bilateral lung hyperplasia, pushing the mediastinum to the right.
E) The mediastinal shift is caused by left lung collapse with compensatory right lung hyperexpansion.

reference.correct_choice_text: The mediastinal shift is caused by volume loss in the right hemithorax with compensatory left lung expansion.

reflection_candidates.json.condition: When CXR shows unilateral lung hyperlucency with reduced vascular markings and small hilum, but side assignment is ambiguous due to rotation or mediastinal shift
reflection_candidates.json.action: Inspect rib spacing and diaphragm position: reduced intercostal space + elevated hemidiaphragm on the same side confirms volume loss (not hyperinflation); correlate with hilum size and vascular tapering
reflection_candidates.json.limitation: Unreliable in severe scoliosis or if diaphragm obscured by gastric air; requires adequate inspiration

reflection_candidates.json.condition: When CXR shows a tubular or nodular opacity extending from the hilum into an upper lobe with adjacent hyperlucent parenchyma
reflection_candidates.json.action: Inspect for decreased vascular markings in the hyperlucent region and absence of volume loss (normal rib spacing, diaphragm position); distinguish from collapse by checking for preserved lung volume
reflection_candidates.json.limitation: Unreliable if inspiratory effort poor or mediastinal shift present; requires PA/lateral correlation
